newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: TENNIS-SAMPRAS FIGHTS THROUGH, IVANISEVIC BEATEN.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-SAMPRAS FIGHTS THROUGH, IVANISEVIC BEATEN.

text.p: World number one Pete Sampras fought his way into the semifinals of the Australian Open on Wednesday, keeping his nerve in a tense five-setter to see off Spanish challenger Albert Costa.

Sampras drew on all his experience as an eight-times grand slam champion to beat Costa, who stormed around the court, running down every ball and conjuring up impossible shots to keep the top seed on the back foot.
Leading with his serve, Sampras powered through the final set to beat the 10th-seeded Costa 6-3 6-7 6-1 3-6 6-2 and book a semifinal clash with Austrian fifth seed Thomas Muster.
"He's fast, he's good, he's got one of the best backhands I've ever seen. On the run, I couldn't believe some of the shots he was getting," Sampras said.
"Now I've got one day off and then it will be Thomas, which will be a war."
Earlier on Wednesday, Muster once more broke Croatian hardman Goran Ivanisevic's grand slam hopes, blasting him out of the tournament in straight sets.
Ivanisevic, the world number four, played like a nervous underdog and made a string of unforced errors as he went down 6-4 6-2 6-3.
"I had a lot of chances I didn't take," he said. "And if you don't take those chances, you're gone."
Ivanisevic has been in the top 10 for more than five years but has never won any of the game's four major events.
With the roof of Centre Court pulled over for the second day -- this time due to torrential rain rather than sun -- Muster appeared to relish the indoor hardcourt conditions.
The super-fit Austrian, shedding the tag of mere clay courter, played a much smarter game, serving smoothly and wearing his opponent down from the baseline.
In the women's draw, Swiss 16-year-old Martina Hingis breezed playfully into the semifinals with a straight sets victory over Romania's Irina Spirlea -- once again making it look easy.

Hingis, seeded number four, made a tentative start, dropping her second service game but immediately broke back and was never troubled again, winning 7-5 6-2 in just 70 minutes. She has yet to drop a set in the tournament.

There was heartbreak for Belgian giant-killer Dominique van Roost, who handed American 14th seed Mary Joe Fernandez her first grand slam semifinal in four years when she retired hurt in the second set because of a pulled abdominal muscle.
Her exit ended Belgium's best grand slam performance after the defeat of 16th seed Sabine Appelmans on Tuesday.
Van Roost had no regrets: "A lot of people think Belgium is French, sometimes you cannot even see the country on the map...I think now they know more about Belgium from the tennis."

A three-day heatwave sent courtside temperatures over 50 degrees Celsius (122 Farenheit) before the rain came on Wednesday, bringing relief not only to players but to firefighters battling forest fires around the city.
Hingis told reporters she had wanted rain.
"I was like a little praying, please," she said. "I have pretty good scores at the indoor tournaments, I have much better control in there, I like that."

Both women's semifinals will be held on Thursday, before the first men's semifinal between world number two Michael Chang of the United States and Spain's Carlos Moya. Sampras and Muster will play on Friday.
